AXI interface definitions typically expose package typedefs in module/interface port declarations. If Vivado IP packager cannot handle package-based port types at the top level, the interface file may need adjustments to use packager-friendly explicit port types.

This include likely contains shared type aliases/macros used to build AXI channel structs and may define or reference burst-related widths. It is a plausible place to introduce a numeric typedef or a $size-based parameter workaround.

Top-level AXI components often use axi_pkg typedefs directly in their module ports. If any packaged IP wrapper is generated from this module, it may need explicit port declarations instead of package typedefs.

Like other top-level components, this file may expose AXI channel types in its ports. Such modules are common candidates for Vivado packaging incompatibilities when package typedefs are used in the port list.
